Reinvesting realized returns into a 103,406 sq ft site next to City Walk, permitted for over 600,000 sq ft of Built-Up Area with plans for approx. AED 1.1 billion scheme

Press Release

DUBAI, UAE — Driven | Forbes Global Properties and its investment partners have acquired a 103,406 sq ft plot adjacent to City Walk, taking the firm’s Dubai portfolio past AED 3 billion. The site, part of the new Al Safa Street Development Project, has permission for over 600,000 sq ft of Built-Up Area and will be developed into an estimated AED 1.1 billion scheme. 

The purchase is funded by capital returned from a series of exits across the city’s prime districts, following the same thesis as the rest of the portfolio. Driven Properties and its partners target prime assets where pricing dislocations leave room to reposition through optimisation, value-add capital expenditure or greenfield development. These mandates provide the flexibility to actively reposition assets, create value and influence pricing benchmarks within their respective markets. The portfolio carries AED 14 billion in gross development value across low-density, design-led projects in Business Bay, the Dubai Water Canal and Jumeirah Bay Island.

“Driven Properties has consistently demonstrated the value that disciplined off-market acquisitions and active asset management can create,” said Abdullah Alajaji, Founder and CEO of Driven | Forbes Global Properties. “We are recycling that capital into sites where we can create value and achieve outsized returns for our group and our investors.”

The sale was facilitated by The Private Collection, a long-standing team within the firm’s brokerage arm, which gives it proprietary access to opportunities. The plot sits near City Walk, with immediate access to Al Safa Street and Sheikh Zayed Road, connecting it to Downtown Dubai, DIFC, Jumeirah Beach, Dubai Design District and Dubai International Airport. Its permitted use was changed from residential to mixed-use, with plans to develop offices, retail and commercial space alongside a private members’ club underway.

Commenting on the transaction, Lina Allaoa, Partner in The Private Collection Team, Driven | Forbes Global Properties, said, “This plot falls in the center of the city. Few remaining plots bring together so many prime districts. Jumeirah, Al Wasl, DIFC, City Walk and Downtown all intersect here. It is the kind of location you build a city-defining landmark on."  

The acquisition comes as investors from Dubai and abroad compete for a shrinking supply of well-located development land. Driven Properties is taking a long-term view on City Walk, where it expects scarce supply, sustained demand and market liquidity to support capital appreciation.

A Track Record of Disciplined Investment

The acquisition follows a series of successful exits across Driven Properties’ Dubai investment portfolio. In August 2026, the firm and its investment partners sold Emaar Square Building 3 in Downtown Dubai for AED 725 million, having acquired the asset for AED 505 million just 21 months earlier. During the holding period, the firm strengthened the building's income profile through leasing and lease restructuring, before completing the exit, which delivered an equity IRR of over 60%.

In April 2026, the firm also exited a 170,000 sq ft landholding in Jumeirah 1. Acquired off-market for AED 119 million in February 2024, the site was subdivided into 22 plots, all of which sold within 22 days for AED 220 million in gross sales.  This represents AED 101 million in gross appreciation over the holding period, equivalent to a 1.85x equity multiple and an estimated annualised IRR of approximately 31%.

The firm and its partners have also established positions across several City Walk buildings, with AED 650 million invested in the area generating an IRR of 40%. Their investments in La Mer have similarly delivered an IRR of 36% on AED 400 million of invested capital. Together, they hold more than AED 2 billion in assets across established prime locations where their conviction is strongest: Jumeirah Bay Island, Jumeirah 1, Meydan, the Dubai Water Canal and City Walk.

Having achieved equity IRRs ranging from 30% to 70% across several investments, Driven | Forbes Global Properties and its partners intend to continue recycling capital into scarce, well-located opportunities across Dubai's established prime districts.
